architecture:
Both files already exist on disk with SPEC-003's, SPEC-005's, SPEC-006's, and SPEC-007's committed content (verified by reading them fresh before drafting this plan: types.rs is 628 lines ending with SPEC-007's DependentsResult struct, tests_types.rs is 2778 lines ending with spec_007_field_level_attribute_absence_pinned_via_source_inspection, 116 passing tests). Each appended block is verified two ways: (1) for types.rs struct/enum/impl declarations, a SCOPED `diff <(grep -B<N> -A<M> '<declaration line>' file) - <<EOF...EOF` extraction, where N/M were computed empirically against a live /tmp fixture built and run during this plan's own drafting (not hand-counted) -- TsconfigMode: -B1 -A4; WorkspaceOptions struct: -B1 -A3; impl WorkspaceOptions: -A18 (no doc comment precedes the `impl` line itself); ExtractRequest: -B2 -A4; for tests_types.rs, a `grep -c 'fn <name>'` existence check (and, for T-004/T-010, an additional existence check on the new helper type/fn name); (2) a real `cargo test` run inside an isolated /tmp fixture crate mirroring this project's src/lib.rs + src/types.rs + src/tests_types.rs layout (same isolation pattern PLAN-001/003/005/006/007 established, needed because the real workspace cannot currently `cargo build`/`cargo test` directly due to a pre-existing io-errors/orin-cargo registry gap unrelated to this plan), asserting the exact cumulative passing-test count after every single task (116 -> 117 -> 118 -> 119 (T-001 through T-004, TsconfigMode) -> 119 -> 120 -> 121 (T-005 through T-007, WorkspaceOptions shape) -> 121 -> 123 -> 124 (T-008 through T-010, WorkspaceOptions methods) -> 124 -> 125 -> 126 -> 127 -> 128 -> 129 -> 130 -> 131 -> 132 (T-011 through T-019, ExtractRequest) -- every task's exact expected count was produced by actually building this plan's entire final state end-to-end in a real fixture crate before this plan was written, per the vector skill's empirical-build recommendation, not estimated). A collision sweep was run against the fully-assembled final file for every grep anchor used in this plan (type/struct/impl declaration lines, test function names, and the new DefaultProbe/CopyProbe/PartialEqProbe/EqProbe/assert_attr_in_item_attribute_run helper names) -- all are confirmed unique (count 1) both in the current real files (as a red-check baseline of 0) and in the final assembled state (count 1), with no collision against any prior spec's existing content.

Reused helpers (defined earlier in tests_types.rs by PLAN-005/006/007, never redefined by this plan): `enum_declaration_block`, `assert_declaration_order` (RustPathAnchor/DependencyTarget/LangData precedent, reused for TsconfigMode's data-carrying-variant declaration order and, generalized to a `pub struct` block per the LineHit precedent, for WorkspaceOptions' and impl WorkspaceOptions' own source blocks); `assert_no_field_level_serde_attribute` (SPEC-007 fix-round-3 precedent, reused verbatim for ExtractRequest's AC-007 field-level-attribute-absence claim); `SerProbe`/`DeProbe` (SPEC-006 precedent, reused verbatim for TsconfigMode's and WorkspaceOptions' AC-002/AC-003 no-Serialize/no-Deserialize claims, with CodeBlock as the positive control in both cases). One helper is new but a trivial, explicitly documented generalization of an existing one: `DefaultProbe` (T-004) generalizes SerProbe/DeProbe's const-specialization technique from Serialize/Deserialize to Default, needed because AC-006 claims TsconfigMode has NO Default impl at all -- a claim only provable via absence-proving const specialization, never via a presence-only generic bound-check function. A second new helper, `assert_attr_in_item_attribute_run` (T-010), generalizes `assert_no_field_level_serde_attribute`'s structural source-inspection approach from field-level serde attributes to a method-level attribute (`#[must_use]`) and, reused directly in T-019, to an item-level attribute (`#[non_exhaustive]`) -- needed because AC-004/AC-005's #[must_use] asymmetry between new and with_tsconfig, and AC-001's #[non_exhaustive] absence claim, each cause only a compile-time effect (a WARNING, or no effect at all) invisible to any runtime assertion, exactly the same category of compile-time-only fact assert_no_field_level_serde_attribute was built to prove structurally rather than behaviorally. The helper scans an item's WHOLE attribute run (every `#[...]`-prefixed line between the nearest preceding `}` and the item itself), not just the single line immediately above the item -- attributes and doc comments are order-independent on a Rust item, so an attribute placed above the item's own doc comment still applies and must still be detected; a naive immediately-preceding-line check misses this and was corrected during this plan's own review.

Copy/PartialEq/Eq absence (part of AC-001's claim, and, per AC-003's `derive(Debug, Clone) only` wording, WorkspaceOptions' Copy/PartialEq claims) IS mechanically pinned by this plan, via CopyProbe/PartialEqProbe/EqProbe (T-004) -- verbatim 4-line generalizations of DefaultProbe's own const-specialization shape, substituting the probed trait -- with SymbolKind (already known to derive Copy, Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize) as the positive control for each. An earlier draft of this plan wrongly conflated this project's `spec_005_derive_lists_pinned` precedent (specific to a *generic bound-check function*, which can only prove trait presence, never absence) with the const-specialization technique this plan's own SerProbe/DeProbe/DefaultProbe lineage already uses -- that technique generalizes to any trait, including Copy/PartialEq/Eq, without modification, and CAN prove absence. #[non_exhaustive] absence (AC-001) is the one genuine exception left unpinned by a probe: the attribute has no effect on matching within the defining crate, so it produces no runtime-observable difference for any const-specialization probe to detect. It is instead pinned structurally, via `assert_attr_in_item_attribute_run` reused directly against types.rs source in T-019 -- a structural check, not a behavioral one, is the only technique available for a compile-time-only, zero-runtime-effect attribute.

T-005 (types.rs: append WorkspaceOptions struct) depends on T-004 (a tests_types.rs task) rather than T-001 (the last prior types.rs task) -- intentional, not an oversight: it keeps this plan's append order deterministic across both shared files (every types.rs task strictly follows the tests_types.rs task pinning the previous types.rs addition), the same serialization discipline every task in this plan already follows.

AC-006's Default-impl distinction from SPEC-007's established pattern (a Default impl that exists but is inert for serde, vs. TsconfigMode's total absence of one) required a genuinely new proof technique, not just a new test using existing techniques -- T-004 builds DefaultProbe as an explicit, documented generalization of SerProbe/DeProbe rather than reaching for a weaker proxy (e.g. grepping types.rs for the literal string 'impl Default', which would be a textual coincidence check, not a compile-time proof). AC-004/AC-005's #[must_use] asymmetry is this plan's other genuinely novel proof obligation: #[must_use] causes only a compile-time WARNING, invisible to any runtime assertion, so T-010 generalizes the field-level-serde-attribute-absence structural technique (SPEC-007's fix round 3) to item-level attributes via assert_attr_in_item_attribute_run, checked to correctly distinguish presence from absence by construction (the helper takes an explicit expect_present bool and is exercised in both directions in the same test: false for new, true for with_tsconfig) rather than only ever checking for presence. The helper scans an item's WHOLE preceding attribute run, not just the single immediately-preceding line, since attributes and doc comments are order-independent on a Rust item -- an earlier draft's narrower check would have missed #[must_use] (or, in T-019, #[non_exhaustive]) placed above the item's own doc comment rather than directly above the item. ExtractRequest's AC-012 UTF-8-path-string wording was independently re-derived against camino 1.2.5's actual src/serde_impls.rs source (not assumed from the spec's own claim) before being written into a test, confirming the Visitor's `expecting` text is exactly "a UTF-8 path string" and that visit_str/visit_string/visit_bytes/visit_byte_buf is the complete method set (no visit_null override, so an explicit JSON null falls through to serde_json's own default invalid-type error using that same expecting text) -- matching AC-012's own claim exactly, including the null case, which this plan's T-016 fixture run confirmed empirically rather than assumed from camino's source alone. AC-009's three-way numeric rule and AC-013's wrong-type matrix (T-014, T-017) both reuse SPEC-007 AC-006's already-established rejection classes verbatim rather than re-deriving them from scratch, per the spec's own explicit citation. All three types' declaration order is pinned by the technique appropriate to whether the type derives Serialize: the include_str!-based enum_declaration_block/assert_declaration_order technique for TsconfigMode and WorkspaceOptions (no Serialize derive, so order is unobservable on the wire -- same situation as SPEC-006's LineHit/RankedBlock/ParentContext), and the simpler exact-serialize-string technique for ExtractRequest (does derive Serialize, so order is directly observable, same as every SPEC-007 type). Copy/PartialEq/Eq absence claims within AC-001/AC-003 are mechanically pinned via CopyProbe/PartialEqProbe/EqProbe (T-004), direct generalizations of the same const-specialization shape SerProbe/DeProbe/DefaultProbe already established in this file, with SymbolKind as positive control -- correcting an earlier draft's conflation of this project's `spec_005_derive_lists_pinned` precedent (specific to a *generic bound-check function*, provably unable to show absence) with the const-specialization technique this plan's own SerProbe/DeProbe/DefaultProbe lineage uses, which generalizes to any trait, including Copy/PartialEq/Eq, without modification. #[non_exhaustive] absence (AC-001) is pinned separately, via the structural source-inspection technique `assert_attr_in_item_attribute_run` (T-010's helper, reused directly against types.rs source in T-019) -- the one genuine exception, since #[non_exhaustive] has no effect on matching within the defining crate and so produces no runtime-observable difference for any probe to detect, matching the same category of compile-time-only fact this plan's #[must_use] asymmetry check (T-010) was already built to prove structurally rather than behaviorally.
